opening_message:
Ticket 1: Timothy Wallace (employee ID E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer. He requested admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so as a full-time employee without ownership, his maximum is write. Admin is above the maximum, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a contractor with basic security training per the Security DB. Contractors with basic training max out at read (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed). He requested admin to Payroll, which is above the max, so I recommend granting read.
reason: Timothy Wallace (E022) requested admin access to Payroll. The two team notes conflict on employment facts: the HR note states he is a full-time Engineer (max write, since Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role and admin requires ownership), while the Security note states he is a contractor with basic security training (max read; write requires advanced training, admin never allowed). Given the unresolved conflict in facts, I apply the more restrictive maximum. Admin is above both maxima, so I grant the lower applicable maximum: read.
